title: NSIC Rc 284 (Sahod Ulan 8) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: NSIC Rc 284 (Sahod Ulan 8): Yield, Maturity, Characteristics
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 284 is an inbred rice for rainfed lowland: about 114 days and 3.7 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 284 is an inbred rice variety for rainfed lowland, known locally as Sahod Ulan 8. The NSIC approved it in 2011. IRRI bred it. It matures in about 114 days and averages 3.7 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 5.7 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 284 yield?

On average it gives 3.7 tonnes per hectare. That is about 74 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 31 rainfed lowland inbreds on the list, which is 3.2 tonnes. But the top yield, 5.7 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 114 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [bacterial leaf blight](/diseases/bacterial-leaf-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [brown planthopper](/pests/brown-planthopper), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits rainfed fields that are seeded directly. So prepare the field when the first rains come, and seed it once the soil holds moisture. Our guide to [land preparation for direct seeded rice](/land-preparation/direct-seeded-rice-land-preparation) shows how. It is recommended for the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 284?
items.a: It is known as Sahod Ulan 8. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 284 take to harvest?
items.a: About 114 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 284?
items.a: It averages 3.7 tonnes per hectare, about 74 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 5.7 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against bacterial leaf blight, tungro, brown planthopper, sheath blight. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
